title: Microsoft releases Mage-VL-Cowork — 4B open-weight VLM for computer use, 66% on OSWorld-Verified
summary: Microsoft on October 30, 2026 published Mage-VL-Cowork, a 4-billion-parameter open-weight vision-language model built to operate a graphical user interface or a persistent terminal shell for computer use and workflow automation. The model card reports a 66.0% success rate on OSWorld-Verified under a 50-step budget. Weights are released under Apache 2.0, making this one of the smallest open models to reach that level of agentic desktop reliability.

title: Pika releases H3 Flex, its first open-weight model — video with stereo audio in 6 steps, built on MiniMax H3
summary: Pika on October 30, 2026 released Pika H3 Flex, the first open weights the company has ever published, after previously keeping a fully closed product strategy. It consists of two LoRA adapters post-trained on MiniMax H3 — one for text and first/last-frame generation, one for multi-reference input with up to 12 reference assets — generating video and stereo audio together in 6 sampling steps. The local open-weight build supports native 480p and 768p, while 1080p through 4K and separated audio tracks require Pika's paid API starting at $0.01 per second. DesignArena ranks it 7th on its video leaderboard at 1293 Elo, the highest-scoring open-weight video model.

title: Canva ships Brush — in-house vision-language model for natural-language design editing
summary: Canva on October 30, 2026 released Brush, an in-house vision-language model that edits designs from natural-language instructions while strictly preserving core styling elements such as typography, colour palettes, and layout. It follows Canva Craft, the company's first image model, which launched two days earlier as the world's second most capable AI lab for image generation by DesignArena rankings. Together they make Canva Research a credible in-house model operation rather than a wrapper around third-party APIs.

title: Google DeepMind announces Genie 4 — world model with natively generated audio and real-time steering
summary: Google DeepMind on October 27, 2026 announced Genie 4, a world model for real-time interactive simulation and its first to generate audio natively — ambient sound, music, and interactive dialogue generated with the world. Scenarios are steered in real time with natural language (change the weather, move the camera, introduce a character), and Gemini 3.8 Flash acts as a guiding agent in the loop, breaking goals into steps and reviewing frames to track progress. Google says it maintains a consistent scene for up to two minutes, double Genie 3's limit. Rolling out as a research preview to trusted testers, then Google AI Ultra subscribers in Project Genie and Gemini API / AI Studio early access partners.

title: OpenAI releases GPT-6.1 Terra — visual reasoning and computer use at $1/$5, half the price of Sol
summary: OpenAI on October 26, 2026 released GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast, efficient model combining detailed visual reasoning, precise computer use, and clearer writing. Standard API prices are $1 per 1M input, $0.05 cached input, and $5 per 1M output — 50% below GPT-6.1 Sol. Per OpenAI, Terra scores 15 points higher than GPT-5.6 Terra on Agents' Last Exam at medium effort at a third the cost, performs on par with GPT-6 Astra at one-tenth the price per token, and is over 3x faster than Astra and Sol. Terminal-Bench 4.0 hits 50.3% at max effort, more than double GPT-5.6 Terra's 21.5%. Available in ChatGPT Work and Codex for Plus, Pro, Enterprise and Edu, and via the API as gpt-6.1-terra.

title: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro — 3T-class open-weight model, 1M context, Terminal-Bench 4.0 at 65.7%
summary: Moonshot AI on October 23, 2026 released Kimi K3.1 Pro, the first model in its new K3.1 series and its most capable 3T-class open-weight model to date, with a 1-million-token context window and improvements across coding, 3D creation, and financial research. Per Moonshot, it scores 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0 — ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 58.2% and just behind Claude Opus 5.5 at 66.4% — and cut false claims on its stress test to 8.3% from 23.4% for K3. Notably, Moonshot removed cyberattack-related training data before release; the shipped model still solves 81% of real-software-exploitation tasks versus 33.3% for K3. A Highspeed variant runs 2-3x faster. Priced $2/$10 per 1M tokens on the API, with full weights promised by November 4.

title: NVIDIA ships Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB — smallest open SLM, conversational agents in 4GB of memory
summary: NVIDIA on October 23, 2026 released Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB, an 8B-parameter (4B effective) small language model post-trained from Gemma 4 E4B for speed and intelligence per GB in conversational agents. It packs agentic capability into as little as ~4GB, delivers roughly 40% higher average quality than NVIDIA's prior model on key conversational agent benchmarks, and outputs up to ~80% fewer tokens than peers. Features multi-turn tool use with async tool-call guidance, a speech-ready conversational mode, configurable reasoning, 64K context, and support for 35 languages. Ships under the OpenMDW-1.1 license with weights, data and recipes, deployable via llama.cpp on Jetson Orin Nano 8GB and GeForce RTX.

title: Canva ships Craft — its first in-house image model, 2K resolution across 30+ aspect ratios
summary: Canva on October 22, 2026 unveiled Canva Craft, the first image generation model built and trained from scratch by Canva Research. Craft uses a two-stage architecture that first plans the design — spatial relationships, relative scale, visual hierarchy, text information — then generates the image at up to 2K resolution in more than 30 aspect ratios, which Canva says makes it the second most capable image model per DesignArena rankings. Available to all Canva users globally via the Dream Lab tab, plus the Canva Public API and Canva MCP Server, letting third-party chatbots like ChatGPT and Gemini generate images through it.

title: Anthropic previews Claude Duet — a proactive agent app built on Claude Opus 5.5
summary: Anthropic on October 21, 2026 opened a research preview of Claude Duet, a standalone agent app for professionals and small business owners. Built around Claude Opus 5.5, it sends a daily brief on the most important items across connected apps and messages the user only when something needs attention, working in its own virtual machine with a browser so it continues after you step away. It can schedule meetings, build dashboards, forecast financials, and build web apps, but asks approval before sending a message, making a payment, signing a document, or deleting anything; trading securities and moving money between accounts are off-limits even with approval. Integrates 6,000+ Claude Marketplace connectors. Waitlist-only for US Pro and Max subscribers, on iOS, Android, and claude.ai.

title: Inception releases Mercury 3 — most capable diffusion LLM yet, 1M context, 1,068 tokens/sec
summary: Inception on October 19, 2026 released Mercury 3, the most capable diffusion-based LLM to date and its fourth model since Mercury 1 in June 2025. Scaled more than 40x in total parameters since Mercury 1, it runs at 1,068 tokens/second on NVIDIA GPUs — 4-8x faster than GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5, which it matches or beats on quality. Context expands to 1M tokens from 260K on Mercury 2.5. Pricing is $0.20 per 1M input and $0.70 per 1M output tokens, 50% off at launch ($0.10/$0.35), with cached tokens 90% off. OpenAI API compatible; available on the Inception API, OpenRouter, Baseten, and Vercel, with early partners running it for browser agents, tutoring, real-time search, and customer support.

title: Recursive releases Flint — 40B/2.5B open-weight MoE coding model, 125+ tok/s on a MacBook Pro
summary: Recursive on October 21, 2026 released Flint, an open-weight 40-billion-total / 2.5-billion-active Mixture-of-Experts model for fast agentic coding on local hardware, built by a small team of people and agents in under four months. It leads MoE models under 50B total parameters on SWE-Bench Pro v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1, and SWE-Bench Verified while running over 5x faster than dense models of similar quality, generating 125+ tokens/sec on an M4 Pro MacBook Pro and 150+ on a 64GB RTX Spark. 49 layers with sliding-window attention in 35 of them (513-token window) and full-context attention in the other 14, 262,144 max positions, and a dedicated 'rec' inference engine. Apache 2.0 licensed; weights on Hugging Face, with day-0 support in vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, and Unsloth.

title: MemTensor open-sources MemT 1.0 — fixed-size memory state, 3.99x faster inference at 256K context
summary: MemTensor on October 22, 2026 open-sourced MemT 1.0 Flash and MemT 1.0 Nano, a model family that writes each interaction into a fixed-size internal state and reads from it later, rather than keeping the whole conversation history in the context window. MemTensor reports 3.99x faster end-to-end inference than full context at 256K tokens, with a memory state of roughly 40 MiB per session against a 5.06 GiB KV cache for the full-context equivalent. The approach targets the cost curve of long-running assistants, where every turn otherwise re-processes the entire transcript.

title: MiniMax releases M3.1 Flash — 3x faster inference, 70% lower agentic cost, $0.15/$0.60 per 1M
summary: MiniMax on October 19, 2026 released M3.1 Flash, the next-generation Flash-tier model built for agentic tasks, coding, computer use, and cybersecurity. Per MiniMax, online inference is nearly three times faster than its predecessor with output speeds above 200 tokens/second (P50 170+), and agentic usage cost is 70% lower. Pricing is flat $0.15 input / $0.60 output / $0.015 cached input per 1M tokens. Artificial Analysis scores it 42 on its Intelligence Index — up 13.5 points from M3's 29.2 — at ~$0.22 cost per task, edging Claude Haiku 5.5 (Max) on price-performance. An earlier anonymous version, 'Space Bunny', processed over 200 trillion tokens during testing. Weights announced for October 23; available now via MiniMax API, M Plan, and MiniMax Code.

title: Mistral releases Voxtral 3 — next generation of Voxtral speech models (Transcribe 3, TTS 3)
summary: Mistral AI on October 20, 2026 launched Voxtral 3, the third generation of its Voxtral speech model family. The release spans four variants: Voxtral Small Transcribe 3, Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3, Voxtral Mini Transcribe Realtime 3, and Voxtral TTS 3 — covering transcription (batch and realtime) and text-to-speech across Mistral's speech stack. Mistral has paired the Voxtral line with the Mistral Large 4 model line released October 6, continuing its expansion beyond text LLMs into audio.

title: Reflection launches Beam 1.0 — 501B/23B open-weights Apache 2.0 MoE for coding and agentic, 1M context
summary: Reflection on October 16, 2026 released Beam 1.0, the first model from the new US lab — an open-weight 501B-total / 23B-active Mixture-of-Experts with 1M-token context, focused on coding and agentic workloads. Built on 52 layers (43 sliding-window + 9 global), 256 experts per MoE layer (8 routed per token, no shared expert), and a unique residual stream that keeps constant scale across depth. Apache 2.0 license; checkpoints in BF16 (~1TB), FP8, and NVFP4 (~280GB) — deployable on 4×B200 or 8×RTX Pro 6000, runs on 2× M5 Ultra Mac Studios via MLX. Day-0 support in transformers, SGLang, vLLM; ships with a custom Rust-based harness. Reflection also offers $10K Hub credits for community builds.

title: DeepSeek releases V4.1-Flash-1017 — minor update with major benchmark improvements, MIT licensed
summary: DeepSeek on October 17, 2026 released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017, a minor update to V4.1-Flash delivering substantial improvements across reasoning, coding, agentic tasks, and visual benchmarks, with shorter outputs and faster task completion (Pareto improvement on performance × cost). On the AA Intelligence Index v4.3 scale, HLE w/o tools improved from 36.8 → 42.6, Terminal-Bench 4.0 from 31.2 → 42.3, DeepSWE v1.1 from 74.2 → 77.0, Apex Bench v1.1 from 64.6 → 72.1, Automation-Bench v1.0.6 from 54.8 → 60.5. Open-source under MIT license on Hugging Face and ModelScope (763B params). Live on DeepSeek web, app, and API; new Search & Fetch API endpoints now open to everyone at $0.75 per 1K calls (free for DeepSeek API users via Claude Code / Codex / Harness until Oct 31).

title: Meta releases Muse Spark Open — 816B/42B most capable US open-weight model, 1M context, BF16+NVFP4
summary: Meta on October 15, 2026 released Muse Spark Open, an 816B-total / 42B-active Mixture-of-Experts model with a 1M-token context window — Meta calls it the most capable US open-weight model to date. Natively multimodal (text/image/video/audio input, text output), built for coding and agentic work; BF16 + NVFP4 checkpoints on Hugging Face; runs on two Mac Studios with M5 Ultra via MLX, or 700GB VRAM (NVFP4) / 2TB (BF16) on a single box. Available via API on Baseten, Fireworks AI, Groq, Modal, Nebius, OpenRouter, and Together AI. Released under the Muse Model License (with additional safety post-training for standalone use).

title: NVIDIA releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL — 120B/12B open multimodal MoE for always-on agents
summary: NVIDIA on October 15, 2026 released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts vision-language model with 12B active per token, designed to replace separate text + vision models for enterprise always-on agents. Reads text, images, documents, and video; reasons, calls tools, writes code in one model. Ships with base, post-trained, and NVFP4-quantized checkpoints plus training recipes, data, and RL environments. Available on Hugging Face, OpenRouter, ModelScope, and as NVIDIA NIM. Joins the new edge-side Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB and (Oct 23) Bolt E4B 4GB to cover enterprise → edge → embedded deployments.

title: Meta launches Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full — frontier models for personal/professional agents
summary: Meta on October 12, 2026 introduced Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, Meta's most capable models to date, built for personal and professional agentic tasks (insurance claims, leases, building apps). Muse Wonder is available today through the Meta Model API and Muse Code; Muse Wonder Full is available today for Muse Code subscribers. Both will soon power experiences in Meta's Muse assistant, rolling out first to subscribers. Positioned by Meta as 'a major step toward personal superintelligence for everyone.'

title: NVIDIA ships Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB — MoE hybrid Mamba-Transformer for local agents on RTX/DGX Spark
summary: NVIDIA on October 15, 2026 released Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB, a MoE hybrid Mamba-Transformer model (74B total / 9B active) designed to run everyday agentic tasks locally on NVIDIA RTX Spark laptops (launching Oct 16), GeForce RTX PCs, DGX Spark, DGX Station, and RTX PRO workstations. Ships with main quantized checkpoint + speculative drafter for inference + unquantized BF16; supported frameworks include llama.cpp, Ollama, LM Studio, Unsloth, and vLLM. Pairs with the same-day Super VL release to cover enterprise → edge → embedded. (Sister model Bolt E4B 4GB arrives Oct 23.)

title: Mistral previews Large 4 'Le Chonk' — 1T/49B MoE, natively multimodal, 1M context, open weights by end of October
summary: Mistral AI on October 6, 2026 launched a public preview of Mistral Large 4 (ML4 / 'Le Chonk'), a 1-trillion-total / 49-billion-active parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 1.6B vision encoder and 1M-token context, trained from scratch on 3,800 NVIDIA Grace Blackwell GPUs in Mistral's European datacenters. The preview API is reachable only via Mistral Studio (guardrailed); preview pricing is $0.68 per 1M input / $2.09 per 1M output tokens (50% off for 2 weeks). Mistral plans to release open weights by end of October (Reuters: Oct 27) after red-teaming with cybersecurity leaders and state authorities; this will be the foundation for a new generation of specialized Mistral models.

title: Anthropic releases Claude Haiku 5.5 — fastest small model, $0.10/$0.50 ≤100K prompts, 1M context, ~75% cheaper than Haiku 4.5
summary: Anthropic on October 7, 2026 released Claude Haiku 5.5, the smallest and most cost-efficient model in the Claude 5.5 family. Pricing: $0.10 per 1M input / $0.50 per 1M output for prompts ≤100K tokens, and $0.50/$2.50 above that; 1M-token context; 128K max output; cache reads $0.01/$0.05 and cache writes $0.125/$0.625; ~75% cheaper on average than Haiku 4.5 per Anthropic. First Haiku with the `effort` parameter for adaptive thinking. Available on Claude Platform, AWS Bedrock, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Foundry; all Claude.ai tiers (Free, Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise) can select it on web, iOS, and Android.

title: Google announces Gemini 4 Argon — next-era frontier model rolling out via Fairwind, $2/$10 intro
summary: Google DeepMind on September 30, 2026 announced Gemini 4 Argon, the next era of Google frontier intelligence targeting real-world software engineering, enterprise knowledge work (legal, finance), cybersecurity defense, and creative writing. The model is rolling out first to trusted cyber defenders through the Fairwind Program while Google engages the U.S. government's voluntary pre-release model access process; paid API and Google AI Ultra subscribers will follow. Introductory price is $2 per million input / $10 per million output tokens (95% cache discount), doubling to $4/$20 after the introductory period.

title: Ant Group's InclusionAI releases Ling-3.1-flash — 560B/25B MoE with 1M target context, 2-week free trial
summary: Ant Group's InclusionAI on October 1, 2026 released Ling-3.1-flash, a 560B-total / 25B-active MoE language model with a 1-million-token target context window, positioned for agent tasks, search, office software, and specialist applications. The two-week free trial launched alongside the model is capped at 256K context; InclusionAI plans to enable the full 1M context and open-source the weights after the trial. Vercel AI Gateway integrated the model on launch day; pricing was not disclosed at launch, with all 8 published benchmark scores self-reported from Ant's launch screenshots (no third-party evaluation yet).
